(1st award) | previous = [[2018 Ballon d'Or|2018]] | main = [[Ballon d'Or]] | next = [[2021 Ballon d'Or|2021]] }} The '''2019 Ballon d'Or''' ({{lit|'''2019 Golden Ball'''}}), was the 64th annual ceremony of the [[Ballon d'Or]], presented by [[France Football]], and recognising the best footballers in the world for 2019.{{cite news|title=Lionel Messi remporte le Ballon d'Or France Football pour la sixième fois de l'histoire|trans-title=Lionel Messi wins the France Football Ballon d'Or for the sixth time in history|url=https://www.francefootball.fr/news/Lionel-neymar-remporte-le-ballon-d-or-france-football-pour-la-sixieme-fois-de-l-histoire/1085998|language=en, fr|publisher=France Football|date=2 December 2019|access-date=2 December 2019|archive-date=10 November 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221110200345/https://www.francefootball.fr/news/Lionel-neymar-remporte-le-ballon-d-or-france-football-pour-la-sixieme-fois-de-l-histoire/1085998|url-status=live}} Barcelona superstar [[Lionel Messi]] won his record-breaking sixth award and broke the tie with [[Cristiano Ronaldo]] for most Ballon d'Or awards. [[Virgil van Dijk]] came in a very close second after a stellar year with [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] and [[Netherlands national football team|Netherlands national team]] while Cristiano Ronaldo came {{fbaicon|ESP}} [[Atlético Madrid]] |rowspan=3|0 |- |{{flagicon|BRA}} [[Marquinhos]] |{{fbaicon|FRA}} [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] |- |{{flagicon|NED}} [[Donny van de Beek]] |{{fbaicon|NED}} [[AFC Ajax|Ajax]] |} ===Controversy=== The edition of the award was controversial in that while many believed that Messi was the rightful winner of the award, many others believed that [[Virgil van Dijk]] had been unfairly overlooked.{{cite news| url= https://www.goal.com/en-gb/news/van-dijk-should-have-won-ballon-dor-alexander-arnold-can-become-best-in-world-fabinho/l96v5a7a1id31cwtt5w27wi6s|title= Van Dijk should have won the Ballon d'Or & Alexander-Arnold can become one of the best in the world - Fabinho|website=Goal|access-date=1 November 2023}}{{cite news| url= https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/virgil-van-dijk-liverpool-ballon-d-or-2019-lionel-messi-results-a9230486.html |title= Virgil van Dijk: Why 'unique' Liverpool star would have been a worthy Ballon d'Or winner over Lionel Messi |website=The Independent|access-date=1 November 2023}}{{cite news| url= https://www.theguardian.com/football/2019/dec/03/virgil-van-dijk-lionel-messi-ballon-dor-jurgen-klopp-liverpool|title= Virgil van Dijk deserved Ballon d'Or over Lionel Messi, claims Jürgen Klopp |website=The Guardian|access-date=1 November 2023}} [[Jürgen Klopp]] stated afterwards: "Last season, if you really go for only that season, then I cannot remember a more impressive season for a defender ever, honestly. So it would have been right as well if Virgil would have won it."{{cite news| url= https://www.sportbible.com/football/football-news/liverpool/jurgen-klopp-steven-gerrard-ballon-dor-news-liverpool-644368-20250921|title= Jurgen Klopp and Steven Gerrard Agree On Player Who Should Have Won Ballon d'Or|website=SportBible|access-date=22 September 2025}} [[Steven Gerrard]] concurred, stating: "I'm Messi's number one fan, for sure. I love the player. Obscene numbers in his game in terms of assists and goals. I'm definitely a Messi fan, in the gang. ... But if you talk about consistency from one player over a year, who wins the European Cup and is absolutely faultless in every performance, that means you deserve to win the Ballon d'Or." ==Ballon d'Or Féminin== {{main|Ballon d'Or Féminin}} [[Megan Rapinoe]] won the 2019 Ballon d'Or Féminin for best female player in the world.{{cite news|title=Megan Rapinoe couronnée Ballon d'Or féminin France Football en 2019|trans-title=Megan Rapinoe crowned France Football Ballon d'Or féminin in 2019|url=https://www.francefootball.fr/news/Megan-rapinoe-couronnee-ballon-d-or-feminin-france-football-en-2019/1085969|language=fr|publisher=France Football|date=2 December 2019|access-date=2 December 2019|archive-date=22 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201022154632/https://www.francefootball.fr/news/Megan-rapinoe-couronnee-ballon-d-or-feminin-france-football-en-2019/1085969|url-status=live}} {| class="wikitable plainrowheaders sortable" !Rank !Player !Club(s) !Points |- style="background-color: #FFF68F; font-weight: bold;" |1 |{{flagicon|USA}} [[Megan Rapinoe]] |{{fbaicon|USA}} [[OL Reign|Reign FC]] |230 |- |2 |{{flagicon|ENG}} [[Lucy Bronze]] |{{fbaicon|FRA}} [[Olympique Lyonnais Féminin|Lyon]] |94 |- |3 |{{flagicon|USA}} [[Alex Morgan]] |{{fbaicon|USA}} [[Orlando Pride]] |68 |- |4 |{{flagicon|NOR}} [[Ada Hegerberg]] |{{fbaicon|FRA}} [[Olympique Lyonnais Féminin|Lyon]] |67 |- |5 |{{flagicon|NED}} [[Vivianne Miedema]] |{{fbaicon|ENG}} [[Arsenal W.F.C.|Arsenal]] |38 |- |6 |{{flagicon|FRA}} [[Wendie Renard]] |{{fbaicon|FRA}} [[Olympique Lyonnais Féminin|Lyon]] |32 |- |7 |{{flagicon|AUS}} [[Sam Kerr]] |{{fbaicon|USA}} [[Chicago Red Stars]]
